summary: R. P. Paranjpye studied under Vaman Shivram Apte until circa 1892. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University from circa 1956 to 1959.

R. Thangaswami Sarma was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Annamalai University and The Madras Sanskrit College. His career included posts at Presidency College, Chennai, Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, ICPR, and Adyar Library and Research Centre (1994–2000).

Working in history, archaeology, and religious studies, R. Venkatraman completed a PhD at Madurai Kamaraj University (1975–1980) under doctoral supervisors N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan. He also served as a Reader at Madurai Kamaraj University.
Rachael Wiseman is a philosopher who studied at the University of York from circa 2004 to 2009. She held a post at the University of Liverpool circa 2016.

Rachel H. Pang, a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, earned her PhD from the University of Virginia by 2015. Circa 2017, she was Lester D. Coltrane III Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College.

Rachelle M. Scott, working in Buddhist and religious studies, completed her dissertation at Northwestern University circa 2001 under George D. Bond and Robert Launay. She held a post at the University of Tennessee circa 2004.

Radhika Herzberger completed her PhD at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal by 1982, working in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Circa 1982, she became Director of Studies at Rishi Valley School.

Rafal Stepien completed a PhD at Columbia University (circa 2009–2015) supervised by Chun-fang Yu and Bernard Faure, working in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was an Exchange Scholar at Harvard and an Academic Visitor at Wadham College in 2012–2013.

Rafał Jan Felbur, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, studied under John R. McRae and Luis Oscar Gómez and earned his PhD at Stanford University by 2018 under doctoral supervisor Paul Harrison.

Raffaele Torella is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Raniero Gnoli. He served as a faculty member at Sapienza University of Rome from 1980 and as a professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale".

Raffaello Orlando, a specialist in Sinology and Buddhist studies, studied at Princeton University from circa 1976 to 1981, earning a PhD under doctoral supervisor Denis Twitchett and teacher Frederic W. Mote.

Raghu Ananthanarayanan completed postgraduate engineering studies at IIT Madras and studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya and T. K. V. Desikachar. His career includes teaching at Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram and serving as visiting faculty at IIM Ahmedabad.

Raghu Vira worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology, studying at the University of the Punjab and Leiden University. From circa 1934 to 1963, he served as chief editor at the International Academy of Indian Culture.

Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar was an Indology and philosophy scholar who served as Ex-Principal at Sir Parashurambhau College (circa 1933–1945) and Director of the Post-Graduate and Research Department at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (circa 1946–1964).
Raghunath Giri, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, studied under Vamacharana Bhattacharya. He held a post as department head (科長) at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Indologist and linguist Rahul Peter Das completed his D. Phil at the University of Hamburg (1978–1993). In 1994, he held the chair for the Philology of Modern Indian Languages at the University of Halle-Wittenberg and guest-professed at Marburg.

Raimon Panikkar, active in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, studied across Europe and India, including Madrid and the Pontifical Lateran University. He held posts at Harvard University (1966–1971) and as professor emeritus at UC Santa Barbara (circa 1987–2010).

Raimond Gaita is a philosopher who studied at the University of Melbourne and the University of Leeds. He held academic posts at King's College London from circa 1989 to 2011 and Australian Catholic University from circa 1993 to 2011.

Rajan Gurukkal, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at the University of Calicut. He served as Director of the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (circa 1990–2008) and held a post at IISc Bengaluru.

Rajendra Chandra Hazra was an Indologist who completed doctoral research under Sushil Kumar De circa 1931–1936. He lectured at Jagannath University and the University of Dhaka before serving as Associate Professor at Sanskrit College and University (1951–1972).
